units.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, he was made Associate Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 入為京兆尹，頃之，加戶部侍郎、兼御史中丞，判度支，委府事於司錄張群、杜亞，綜大體，議論號為稱職。
units.en: Recalled to serve as metropolitan governor of Chang'an, he soon added the titles of vice minister of revenue and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, with charge of the revenue bureau. He left routine office work to Zhang Qun and Du Ya as recorders while he kept the broad direction in hand, and contemporaries judged his policy judgments sound.
units.literal: He entered the capital as Metropolitan Governor; shortly thereafter he was additionally appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, with charge of revenue; he entrusted administrative affairs to Clerks Zhang Qun and Du Ya, while he handled overall policy, and his deliberations were said to be competent.

units.zh: 時史朝義盜據東都，寄理長水。
units.en: With Shi Chaoyi holding the Eastern Capital, Yan governed from Changshui as his provisional seat.
units.literal: At that time Shi Chaoyi was occupying the Eastern Capital by force, so he administered affairs from Changshui.

units.zh: 宰相楊炎遇之頗厚，召入左司郎中、京兆少尹，遷大尹。
units.en: Chief Minister Yang Yan treated him generously, brought him to court as bureau director in the Left Secretariat and junior magistrate of the capital district, and then promoted him to chief magistrate.
units.literal: Chief Minister Yang Yan treated him very generously, summoned him in as bureau director in the Left Secretariat and junior magistrate of the capital district, and promoted him to chief magistrate.

units.zh: 蓋唐室自懿宗失政，天下亂離，故武宗以下實錄，不傳於世。
units.en: From Tang Yizong's loss of rule the realm shattered; veritable records from Wuzong down no longer circulated.
units.literal: It is that from Emperor Yizong of Tang the government was lost and the realm torn apart; therefore veritable records from Emperor Wuzong down were not transmitted in the world.

units.zh: 然暴橫少恩，杖前部尉以逞憾，觀察使王緯以聞，德宗不省。
units.en: Yet he was brutal and unforgiving: he had a former subordinate commandant flogged to settle a personal score. Observation commissioner Wang Wei reported it, but Emperor Dezong paid no heed.
units.literal: Yet he was violent and overbearing and short on kindness; he beat a former subordinate commandant to vent a grudge. Observation commissioner Wang Wei reported this, but Emperor Dezong took no notice.

units.zh: 帝晚務姑息，頔所奏建，無不開允。
units.en: In his later years the emperor favored appeasement, and every proposal Di submitted won approval.
units.literal: The emperor in his later years pursued indulgence and forbearance; whatever Di memorialized and proposed was invariably approved.

units.zh: 俄擅以兵取鄧州，天子未始誰何。
units.en: Before long he seized Dengzhou by force on his own authority, and the emperor never called him to account.
units.literal: Soon he on his own authority took Dengzhou by force, and the Son of Heaven never once held him to account.

units.zh: 智興能駛步，奉表，不數日至京師告急，德宗出朔方軍五千擊納，解去，自是為徐特將。
units.en: Zhixing could run at great speed; he carried a memorial and reached the capital within days to report the crisis. Dezong dispatched five thousand Shuofang troops against Na and lifted the siege; from then on Zhixing was a special general of Xuzhou.
units.literal: Zhixing could run swiftly; he bore a memorial and in only a few days reached the capital to report the emergency. Dezong sent out five thousand Shuofang troops to strike Na, and the siege was lifted; from then on he was a special general of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 德宗既厭兵，大抵刺史重代易，至歷年不徙。
units.en: After the emperor wearied of campaigning, prefects were usually turned over often—though some lingered in office for years on end.
units.literal: Once Emperor Dezong grew weary of warfare, for the most part prefects were frequently rotated, yet some went years without transfer.

units.zh: 德宗立，召還。
units.en: Dezong's accession brought his recall to court.
units.literal: When Emperor Dezong acceded, he was recalled.

units.zh: 先時，淮南節度陳少遊首稱臣於李希烈，鳳翔將李楚琳殺節度使張鎰以應硃泚，鎰判官韋臯先知隴州留後，首殺豳叛卒數百人，不應楚琳。
units.en: Earlier, Huainan military governor Chen Shaoyou was the first to declare himself subject to Li Xilie. Fengxiang general Li Chulin killed military governor Zhang Yi to join Zhu Ci. Zhang Yi's staff judge Wei Gao, who had earlier served as acting rear commander of Long prefecture, was the first to kill several hundred mutinous soldiers from Bin and refused to follow Chulin.
units.literal: Earlier, Huainan military governor Chen Shaoyou was the first to declare himself subject to Li Xilie; Fengxiang general Li Chulin killed military governor Zhang Yi to respond to Zhu Ci; Yi's staff judge Wei Gao, who had earlier been acting rear commander of Long prefecture, was the first to kill several hundred mutinous soldiers from Bin and did not respond to Chulin.

units.zh: 韋臯名宦最卑，特建忠義。
units.en: Wei Gao's official rank was the most humble, yet he specially established loyalty and righteousness.
units.literal: Wei Gao's official name and rank were the most humble, yet he specially established loyalty and righteousness.

units.zh: 復江南使回，與宰相同對訖，復獨留，奏曰：「陛下自返宮闕，勛臣已蒙官爵，唯旌善懲惡，未有區分。
units.en: When Fu returned from his Jiangnan mission, after answering together with the chief ministers he alone remained and memorialized, saying, "Since Your Majesty returned to the palace, meritorious ministers have already received ranks and titles, yet in honoring good and punishing evil there has been no distinction.
units.literal: When Fu returned from his Jiangnan mission, after answering together with the chief ministers he alone remained and memorialized, saying: 'Since Your Majesty returned to the palace, meritorious ministers have already received ranks and titles, yet in honoring good and punishing evil there has been no distinction.

units.zh: 請令韋臯代少遊，則天下明然知逆順之理。」
units.en: I request that Wei Gao be ordered to replace Chen Shaoyou, so that All Under Heaven will clearly understand the principle of rebellion and submission."
units.literal: I request that Wei Gao be ordered to replace Shaoyou, and then All Under Heaven will clearly know the principle of rebellion and submission.'

units.zh: 鎮州王承宗死，弘正自魏移領鎮州。
units.en: When Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died, Hongzheng left Wei to assume command of Zhenzhou.
units.literal: Wang Chengzong of Zhen prefecture died; Hongzheng moved from Wei to take charge of Zhen.

units.zh: 咸通中，從討龐勳，以功為振武都校。
units.en: In the Xiantong era he took part in the suppression of Pang Xun and, for his service, was appointed metropolitan commandant of Zhenwu.
units.literal: During the Xiantong period he followed the campaign against Pang Xun and, for merit, was made metropolitan commandant of Zhenwu.

units.zh: 父德成，初為天寧軍使，從獻祖討龐勳，以功授朔州刺史。
units.en: His father Decheng had first served as military commissioner of Tianning. He followed the Offering Ancestor against Pang Xun and, for his service, was made prefect of Shuozhou.
units.literal: His father Decheng was first military commissioner of Tianning. He followed the Offering Ancestor in the campaign against Pang Xun and, for merit, was appointed prefect of Shuozhou.

units.zh: 遠祖沒諾幹，唐至德中，事鎮州節度使王武俊為騎將。
units.en: His distant ancestor Mo Nuogan served as a cavalry commander under Wang Wujun, military governor of Zhenzhou, during the Zhide reign of Tang.
units.literal: A remote ancestor, Mo Nuogan, during the Zhide era of Tang served the Zhenzhou military governor Wang Wujun as a mounted commander.

units.zh: 武俊嘉其勇幹，畜為假子，號王五哥，其後子孫以王為氏。
units.en: Wujun admired his courage and competence, took him as an adoptive son, and called him Fifth Brother Wang; his descendants thereafter adopted Wang as their clan surname.
units.literal: Wujun admired his courage and ability, raised him as an adopted son, and called him Fifth Brother Wang; later generations took Wang as their surname.

units.zh: 元和中，田弘正討李師道，令憲誠以先鋒四千人濟河，累下其城柵。
units.en: During the Yuanhe reign, when Tian Hongzheng marched against Li Shidao, he sent Xiancheng ahead with four thousand vanguard troops to cross the Yellow River and take one fortified camp after another.
units.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao and ordered Xiancheng to cross the river with four thousand vanguard troops, repeatedly capturing his fortified camps.

units.zh: 進滔客寄於魏，委質軍門，事節度使田弘正。
units.en: Jintao had settled in Wei as an outsider, pledged himself to the army, and served under the military governor Tian Hongzheng.
units.literal: Jintao lived as a guest in Wei, pledged himself to the army gate, and served the military governor Tian Hongzheng.

units.zh: 居數月，爲王廷湊所殺，遂以兵叛。
units.en: Within a few months Hongzheng was murdered by Wang Tingcou, who then rose in armed rebellion.
units.literal: After several months he was killed by Wang Tingcou, who then rebelled with troops.

units.zh: 朝廷以弘正子布爲魏博節度使，領兵討伐，俾復父冤。
units.en: The court made Hongzheng's son Bu military governor of Weibo and sent him to campaign against the rebels, that he might avenge his father's death.
units.literal: The court appointed Hongzheng's son Bu as military governor of Weibo and led troops to punish the rebels, so that he might avenge his father.

units.zh: 弘正奉詔討鄆州，破李師道，時進滔爲衙內都知兵馬使，以功授兼侍御史。
units.en: When Hongzheng marched on Yanzhou by imperial order and broke Li Shidao, Jintao was chief controller of horse and foot in the headquarters guard and was made concurrent Attending Censor for his service.
units.literal: Hongzheng received the edict to campaign against Yanzhou and defeated Li Shidao; at the time Jintao was Chief Controller of Cavalry and Infantry within the headquarters guard, and for his merit was appointed concurrent Attending Censor.

units.zh: 乃以吏部尚書張弘靖兼平章事，代弘鎮宣武。
units.en: Minister of Personnel Zhang Hongjing was made associate grand councilor to replace Hong as military governor of Xuanwu.
units.literal: Thereupon Minister of Personnel Zhang Hongjing was made Associate Grand Councilor to replace Hong in governing Xuanwu.

units.zh: 溫固執，文宗諭而止。
units.en: Wei held firm until Wenzong instructed him to stop.
units.literal: Wei persisted; Emperor Wenzong instructed him and he desisted.

units.zh: 開成初，文宗欲以真源、臨真二公主降士族，謂宰相曰：「民間脩婚姻，不計官品而上閥閱。
units.en: Early in Kaicheng, Wenzong meant to marry the Princesses Zhenyuan and Linzhen into great clans and told his chief ministers: "Common folk arranging marriages care nothing for office and everything for pedigree.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era, Emperor Wenzong wished to marry the Princesses Zhenyuan and Linzhen to gentry families and said to the chief ministers: "Among the people in arranging marriages, they do not consider official rank but esteem clan pedigree.

units.zh: 帝聞異之，轉太仆、衛尉二少卿，歷左右金吾大將軍。
units.en: The emperor, struck by his words, moved him through the vice directorships of the Stud and Guard courts and then the Left and Right commands of the Golden Guard.
units.literal: The emperor heard this with surprise and transferred him to the two vice directorships of the Court of the Imperial Stud and the Court of the Imperial Guard, then through the Left and Right Golden Guard commands.

units.zh: 久之，復拜司農卿，入謝，帝曰：「卿用法深，信乎？」
units.en: Long afterward he was reappointed Director of the National Granaries; at his audience of thanks the emperor asked, "They say you enforce the law harshly—is it true?"
units.literal: After a long while he was again appointed Director of the Court of the National Granaries; entering to give thanks, the emperor said: "You apply the law with severity—is that so?"

units.zh: 帝許之。
units.en: The emperor agreed.
units.literal: The emperor consented.
